title: The Transformative Lesson Formatter
description: Converts professional experiences into high-engagement LinkedIn narratives with real takeaways
prompt:
Write a LinkedIn post sharing 3 lessons I've learned from [describe a recent client project or business experience].

Rules:
- Each lesson must be specific and actionable, not generic
- Include a concrete takeaway for [target audience, e.g. small business owners / developers / designers]
- Open with a hook that stops the scroll — not 'I'm excited to share'
- End with a question that invites comments
- Keep it under 200 words
- No bullet point lists — write in short punchy paragraphs
useCase: Converting everyday professional experiences into highly engaging, relatable thought-leadership narratives that create emotional connection.

title: The Common Problem Solver
description: Positions you as an authority by addressing a pain point your audience struggles with every day
prompt:
Write a LinkedIn post explaining why many [target audience, e.g. service providers / freelancers / startup founders] struggle with [specific problem] and how to overcome it.

Structure:
1. Open by naming the pain — make the reader feel seen
2. Explain WHY this problem happens (the root cause most people miss)
3. Give 2-3 specific, actionable solutions
4. Close with a line that positions you as someone who has solved this

Keep it under 250 words. Conversational tone. No corporate speak.
useCase: Positioning the author as an industry authority by directly addressing and resolving ubiquitous audience pain points.

title: The Client Success Story Arc
description: Builds a compelling before/after client transformation post with measurable results and social proof
prompt:
Draft a LinkedIn client transformation post.

Details to include:
- Client situation BEFORE working with me: [describe the problem]
- What we did together: [describe the solution or service]
- Measurable result AFTER: [describe the outcome with numbers if possible]

Rules:
- Focus on the client's journey, not on how great I am
- Use specific numbers wherever possible (% increase, time saved, revenue gained)
- Do not make it sound like an ad — make it sound like a story
- End with one insight other people can take away from this result
- Under 200 words
useCase: Building unshakeable credibility and social proof through data-backed, narrative case studies that prove competence.

title: The Confusing Topic Breakdown
description: Simplifies a complex industry topic so even non-experts can understand and engage
prompt:
Write a LinkedIn post simplifying [confusing industry topic] so a complete non-expert can understand it.

Rules:
- Open with why this topic matters to your audience (make them care first)
- Use one analogy to explain the core idea
- Break it down in plain language — no jargon unless immediately explained
- End with one practical implication: 'What this means for you is...'
- Target length: 150-200 words
- Tone: intelligent but approachable, not condescending
useCase: Expanding reach by democratizing complex industry jargon for a broader, non-technical audience, making the author highly approachable.

title: The Industry Myth Debunker
description: Creates conversation-starting posts by challenging a common misconception in your industry
prompt:
Create a LinkedIn post that challenges a common myth in my industry: [industry or niche]

My chosen myth: [state the myth you want to debunk]

Structure:
1. State the myth boldly — make people who believe it feel called out (politely)
2. Explain why this myth exists and why people believe it
3. Reveal the actual truth with evidence or personal experience
4. End with a question to spark debate in the comments

Tone: confident, not preachy. You can be slightly controversial but not offensive. Under 200 words.
useCase: Sparking algorithmic engagement and prolonged discourse by leveraging mild, professional controversy and challenging misconceptions.

title: The Headline Optimizer
description: Creates a keyword-rich LinkedIn headline that captures attention and ranks in recruiter searches
prompt:
Help me create a LinkedIn headline that effectively communicates my experience, qualifications, and unique value.

Consider:
- Incorporating keywords relevant to my industry (from my resume below)
- Showcasing my passion or mission statement
- Making it a snapshot that captures attention immediately — not a job title
- It should answer: 'Why should someone click on my profile?'

Generate 3 headline options ranging from professional to bold.

My resume / background: [paste your resume or key details here]
useCase: Ensuring the profile ranks highly in recruiter search queries while immediately communicating distinct professional value.

title: The 150-Word Summary Crafter
description: Writes a conversational LinkedIn About section that feels human, not like a corporate resume
prompt:
Craft a concise and compelling summary for my LinkedIn About section.

Requirements:
- Highlight my professional journey, key skills, and what makes me unique
- Tone: conversational and warm — NOT a resume rewrite
- Must NOT exceed 150 words
- Start with something other than 'I am a...'
- End with a clear call to action (what I want people to do after reading)

My background: [paste your resume or write a brief description of your experience]
useCase: Creating an easily digestible, highly engaging professional bio that avoids the sterile, corporate tone of traditional resumes.

title: The Experience Section Impact Generator
description: Rewrites job descriptions into metric-driven achievement statements that prove organizational impact
prompt:
Craft impactful entries for my LinkedIn Experience section that go beyond job descriptions.

For each role, share:
- Not just what I did — but HOW my contributions made a measurable difference
- Action verbs that show initiative and ownership
- Quantified achievements wherever possible (%, $, time saved, users impacted)
- Context that highlights the value I brought to the organization

Do NOT just rephrase my job description. Transform duties into achievements.

My resume / job history: [paste your experience here]
useCase: Translating static job duties into dynamic, metric-driven achievements that prove organizational impact and historical success.

title: The Vulnerable Business Story
description: Writes an authentic post about a professional failure or challenge — the content type that builds the deepest trust
prompt:
Write a LinkedIn post about a time I faced a significant challenge or failure in [work / business / career].

Details: [describe the situation briefly]

Structure:
1. Open with the moment things went wrong — put the reader in the scene
2. Describe what I tried that didn't work
3. What I finally learned from it (the real insight, not a cliché)
4. How it changed how I work or think now

Rules:
- Be genuinely vulnerable — not performatively vulnerable
- Do NOT end with 'Everything happens for a reason'
- Under 220 words
- No bullet points — narrative paragraphs only
useCase: Fostering deep trust and humanizing the professional brand, as vulnerability heavily outperforms sterile corporate updates algorithmically.
